newsitem.title: ITALY: Castrol Italiana 1996 sales up,profit flat.
newsitem.headline: Castrol Italiana 1996 sales up,profit flat.

text.p: Castrol Italiana SpA, the Italian unit of British lubricants maker Burmah Castrol Plc, said its 1996 turnover rose to 121.06 billion lire from a previous 118.79 billion while net profit was 9.63 billion against 10.64 billion.

The company said last year marked a consolidation period in a generally "lazy" Italian market. But the first six months of 1997 showed "significant growth" and forecasts for full year results were "definitely positive."
Castrol Italiana managing director Cesare Guaita said he was satisfied with the 1996 results given the background of a strong market downturn.

"The continuous technological innovation which characterises Castrol products is the keystone of our success. In fact most of our profit comes from sales of new lubrificants, all launched on the market in the last five years," he said.
He told reporters at a press briefing that Castrol had an Italian market share of four to five percent and was second only to Germany in Europe in terms of profit.
He said Castrol in Italy was closely linked to racing, both cars and powerboats but above all motorcycle racing which has a long and proud tradition in the country.

He noted Castrol sponsored the Williams Formula One motor-racing team and that Italian motorcycle racing champion Max Biaggi was now with Castrol and Honda, with which the company had a relationship going back 20 years. In fact, the Japanese firm's only motorcycle plant is in Italy, he added.
Castrol was looking to expand and was prepared to make acquisitions in Italy, although likely to be fairly small, as long as they added value to the business, Guaita said.

Burmah Castrol, which posted a 10 percent rise in its 1996 profit, expects to keep expanding globally, especially in Asia and the Pacific from where it expects to see some 50 percent of total profits by the year 2000 against 40 percent currently.
Burmah Castrol profit after tax before exceptional items rose to 148.7 million sterling, up from 135.0 million in 1995.

Castrol Italiana, founded in 1955, has two production centres at Cornaredo, outside Milan which concentrates on engine products, and at Mappano, Turin which produces industrial lubricants primarily for the metalworking industry.
